The doctrine of force majeure is a legal concept that excuses a party from fulfilling their obligations in a contract if an event beyond their control makes it impossible to do so.

The term "force majeure"
literally means "superior force" and comes from French civil law.

As per the dictionary, the term includes both acts of nature (e.g. floods and hurricanes) and acts of people (e.g. riots, strikes and wars).
